description: Nutrient and unit registry for catalog contract v1. Nutrient ids are the only keys a product version's nutrients object may carry, and a value's unit must be one of the units listed for that nutrient. Every unit symbol here is a symbol the iOS UnitRegistry knows, spelled the same way, so a contract-valid document always decodes in the app. Factors are exact decimal strings to the canonical unit of the unit's own dimension and are powers of ten, so a conversion within a dimension is exact. Mass to volume and volume to mass need a stated density; international units never convert; count units need a stated portion.
notes: Each symbol has exactly one spelling, the one the iOS UnitRegistry uses. A provider's ug, ml, l or iu is normalised to mcg, mL, L or IU by the importer before a record is published; the aliases are not part of the wire contract.
Energy is stated in kcal only. kJ is not a v1 unit: the app does not know it, and 1 kJ in kcal has no finite decimal form. An importer converts a kJ-only label before publishing.
A nutrient's units are the units of its dimension. Vitamin A and vitamin D also accept IU, because labels state them that way; an IU amount stays in IU and never converts to a mass.
A serving is stated in a mass, volume or count unit, never in kcal or IU.

Count units other than the canonical serving have no factor: converting between count units is refused, and converting between a count unit and a mass or volume unit needs a portion definition, plus a density when the portion is stated in the other of mass and volume.
